verification: Updated native-client POST parity verified against AWS protected preview and both Vercel production projects at the same committed revision.

ordinaryClientAWSPostParity.proof: Actual production URLSession requests are intercepted after native code has set the digest, verified against their exact body, then forwarded unchanged except host and existing operator-only AWS preview Authorization. No test-supplied payload hash.
ordinaryClientAWSPostParity.oversizeBehavior: 65537 bytes and encoded multi-byte parser overflow fail in native preparation before URLSession transport. Streams/missing owned POST bodies rejected.
ordinaryClientAWSPostParity.existingInstalledVersions: Website deployment does not update older native clients. Production client URLs remain on Vercel; AWS stays operator protected.

buildHost: Current owned Mac; Next/OpenNext/Vercel prebuilt output built locally. Existing provider deployment finalization only.

checks.nativeRequest: PASS actual URLSession requests and bounded-body cases

dependencies.scope: Production and development dependencies; compatible transitive fixes, not omit-dev audit.

singleOwnerEffects: No jobs, webhooks, payments, notification jobs, databases or new hosted services added. AWS operator-only preview; production routing remains Vercel.
providerRetention: No application event database/content logs; OpenAI store:false with separate provider operational retention. Photo search terms occur in GET URLs and may enter hosting logs. Salted address counters have a one-minute window and expire on later requests or instance termination. AWS application diagnostic retention verified seven days; no invented retention for Vercel or providers.
limitations: Actual native UI/device workflows and App Store submission are not established by headless URLSession tests or archives.
tvOS development-signed archive verified; iOS archive is unsigned. Distribution upload remains separate.
AWS remains a protected preview. Sustained parallel operation, rollback and cutover readiness need the scheduled migration review.
Existing per-instance throttles are not distributed quotas or client authentication.
Older installed native versions are not changed by deployment.

priorParityCorrection.reason: AWS provider POST probes explicitly added x-amz-content-sha256. Ordinary shipped native/browser clients do not add this header. Plain OAC requires it for body-bearing requests; those probe results verify provider execution only, not ordinary-client POST parity. AWS functional parity and cutover readiness are NOT verified until the signing mode/client behavior is corrected and retested.

syntheticProviderCallsThisCorrection.explanation: One native end-to-end check on each of three hosts before deployment and again after; boundary/invalid-body checks do not call providers.
